newsitem.title: CROATIA: PRESS DIGEST - Croatian weekly - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Croatian weekly - July 23.

text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian weekly Globus. Reuters has not verifired these stories and does not vauch for their accuracy.

- After news reports that the Vatican hid gold of the Croatian Ustasha regime after World War II, daughter of Ustasha leader Ante Pavelic claims her father never took part in any such financial transactions, nor did his family use the gold.

- At last weekend's meeting between Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and U.S. ambassador to the United Nations Bill Richardson, Croatia has at last risen above its lowest ever levels in relations with America.

- Slovenia supports Croatian integration into NATO and European institutions but if the European Union wants to stop on Slovenia's southern border Slovenia says it will act without altruism and join alone.

- Vitez (in central Bosnia) has become a ghost town with deserted streets, after British Special Air Service units swept the town in search of indicted Bosnian Croat war criminals, presumed to be living there.

- Croatia will not agree to finance the (Catholic) church by way of new taxes says government minister Jure Radic, head of a commission for relations with the church. He was responding to recent controversial allegations surrounding the appointment of Zagreb's new Archbishop.
- Globus claims it has documentation on all Bosnian Moslems and foreign Islamic fighters who, during the Croat-Moslem war in 1993, killed 415 unarmed Croats in 21 different locations.

- My biggest succes will be the role of boxer Mohammed Ali, who told me I am good-looking enough to portray him, says African American upcoming movie star Will Smith. -- Zagreb Newsroom +385 1 455 7075
